quests.instruction: A row of shapes goes triangle, circle, square, triangle, circle, square, triangle. Which shape comes next?
quests.hint: Find the group of shapes that repeats, then see where the row stops.
quests.explanation: The group triangle, circle, square repeats. The row stops after a triangle, so the circle comes next.
quests.funFact: A group of items that repeats in a pattern is called the pattern's unit.

quests.instruction: A pattern goes star, star, heart, star, star, heart, star. Which shape comes next?
quests.hint: Find the repeating unit, then check how far into the next copy of it the row has reached.
quests.explanation: The unit is star, star, heart. The row has used one star of the next unit, so another star comes next.
quests.funFact: Patterns with two of one thing and one of another are often found in music beats.

quests.instruction: A pattern repeats the unit square, triangle, triangle. What is the 7th shape?
quests.hint: Write out the shapes in order up to the 7th.
quests.explanation: The shapes go square, triangle, triangle, square, triangle, triangle, square. The 7th shape starts a new unit, so it is a square.
quests.funFact: The 7th shape is the first shape of the third unit.

quests.instruction: One shape is missing in this pattern: circle, square, ?, circle, square, triangle, circle, square, triangle. Which shape is missing?
quests.hint: Look at how the other groups of three end.
quests.explanation: Each group of three is circle, square, triangle, so the missing shape is a triangle.
quests.funFact: Looking at other copies of the unit helps fill in a missing piece.

quests.instruction: One shape is missing in this pattern: hexagon, hexagon, circle, circle, hexagon, ?, circle, circle. Which shape is missing?
quests.hint: The unit has two of each shape. Count to the missing spot.
quests.explanation: The unit is hexagon, hexagon, circle, circle. The missing shape is the second hexagon in the second unit.
quests.funFact: Patterns with two of each, like AABB, are common in tile designs.

quests.instruction: The pattern square, triangle, triangle repeats. Among the first 10 shapes, how many are triangles?
quests.hint: Write the first 10 shapes in order, then count the triangles.
quests.explanation: The first 10 shapes are square, triangle, triangle, square, triangle, triangle, square, triangle, triangle, square. There are 6 triangles.
quests.funFact: In every full unit of 3 shapes there are 2 triangles.

quests.instruction: Look at this pattern: 1 triangle, then 2 triangles, then 3 triangles, then 4 triangles. What is the rule?
quests.hint: Compare each step with the one before it.
quests.explanation: Each step has one more triangle than the step before, so the rule is to add one each time.
quests.funFact: A rule that adds the same amount each time makes what is called a growing pattern.

quests.instruction: A pattern uses 1 square, then 2 squares, then 4 squares, then 8 squares. How many squares will the next step have?
quests.hint: Find what the numbers do each step: do they add the same amount, or something else?
quests.explanation: Each step has twice as many squares as the one before, so the next step has 8 × 2 = 16 squares.
quests.funFact: A pattern that doubles grows very fast. Doubling 1 ten times gives 1,024.

quests.instruction: The shapes triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon follow a pattern. If it continues, how many sides will the 5th shape have?
quests.hint: Look at how the number of sides changes from one shape to the next.
quests.explanation: The number of sides goes 3, 4, 5, 6, adding one each time, so the 5th shape has 7 sides.
quests.funFact: A shape with seven sides is called a heptagon.

quests.instruction: An arrow points up, then right, then down, then left, then up again. Which way will it point next?
quests.hint: Each arrow is a quarter turn from the one before. Which way is the turn?
quests.explanation: The arrow turns a quarter turn clockwise each time: up, right, down, left. After up comes right.
quests.funFact: Clock hands turn in the same direction as this arrow pattern.

quests.instruction: A triangle with three equal sides has a dot on its top corner. It is turned one third of a full turn clockwise, three times in a row. Where is the dot after the third turn?
quests.hint: Three thirds make a whole turn.
quests.explanation: Three thirds of a turn make one full turn, which returns the triangle, and the dot, to where it started.
quests.funFact: A full turn always brings any shape back to its starting position.

quests.instruction: A pattern alternates a red circle and a blue square, starting with a red circle. What is the 8th shape?
quests.hint: Even places hold the same kind of shape as the 2nd place.
quests.explanation: Odd places are red circles and even places are blue squares. The 8th place is even, so it is a blue square.
quests.funFact: Alternating patterns like this one are called AB patterns.

quests.instruction: A pattern shows 1 circle, then 2 squares, then 3 triangles, then 4 circles, then 5 squares. What comes next?
quests.hint: Two things change: the number and the shape. Follow each one separately.
quests.explanation: The numbers go up by one each time, and the shapes repeat circle, square, triangle. After 5 squares come 6 triangles.
quests.funFact: Patterns that change two things at once are easier to spot if you follow each change on its own.

quests.instruction: Row 1 has 1 square, Row 2 has 3 squares, and Row 3 has 5 squares. How many squares will Row 4 have?
quests.hint: Find how many squares are added from one row to the next.
quests.explanation: Each row has 2 more squares than the row before: 1, 3, 5, 7. Row 4 has 7 squares.
quests.funFact: Adding 2 each time gives the odd numbers: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, and so on.

quests.instruction: A pattern of squares has 1 square, then 4 squares in a 2 by 2 square, then 9 squares in a 3 by 3 square, then 16 squares in a 4 by 4 square. How many squares will the next big square have?
quests.hint: Think about how many rows there are and how many squares are in each row.
quests.explanation: The next big square is 5 by 5, which has 5 × 5 = 25 small squares.
quests.funFact: Numbers like 1, 4, 9, 16, and 25 are called square numbers because they make square shapes.

quests.instruction: A pattern should repeat circle, triangle, square. A child drew circle, triangle, square, circle, square, triangle. Which shape is the first one that is wrong?
quests.hint: Check each shape against the unit, one at a time, from the start.
quests.explanation: The first four shapes are correct. The fifth should be a triangle, but a square was drawn, so the fifth shape is the first mistake.
quests.funFact: Checking a pattern from the beginning helps you find the first mistake.

quests.instruction: Which list follows the rule two triangles, then one circle, repeating?
quests.correctAnswer: Triangle, triangle, circle, triangle, triangle, circle
options: Triangle, triangle, circle, triangle, triangle, circle
Triangle, circle, circle, triangle, circle, circle
Triangle, triangle, circle, circle, triangle, triangle
quests.hint: Check the first three shapes, then check that the group repeats.
quests.explanation: The rule makes the group triangle, triangle, circle, and this list repeats it twice. The other lists use different groups.
quests.funFact: A rule tells you what the repeating group is, and the group tells you the whole pattern.

quests.instruction: The pattern square, triangle, square, triangle continues. Ben says the 10th shape is a square. Is he right?
quests.correctAnswer: No, the 10th shape is a triangle
options: Yes, the 10th shape is a square
No, the 10th shape is a triangle
No, the 10th shape is a circle
quests.hint: Squares are in odd places. Is 10 odd or even?
quests.explanation: Squares are in the 1st, 3rd, 5th places, and so on, which are odd places. The 10th place is even, so it is a triangle.
quests.funFact: Even and odd places can decide an alternating pattern.

quests.instruction: The first 12 shapes follow the repeating unit circle, square, triangle. How many circles are there?
quests.hint: How many full units fit into 12 shapes?
quests.explanation: Each unit has 3 shapes and 12 ÷ 3 = 4 units, with one circle in each unit, so there are 4 circles.
quests.funFact: Dividing by the length of the unit tells you how many times the pattern repeats.

quests.instruction: The pattern triangle, triangle, square repeats. What is the 20th shape?
quests.hint: Find where the 20th shape falls in its group of three.
quests.explanation: 18 shapes make 6 full units, so the 19th shape is the first triangle of the next unit and the 20th is the second triangle.
quests.funFact: Counting full units first and then the leftover is a fast way to find shapes far along a pattern.

quests.instruction: In the repeating pattern square, circle, triangle, circle, which of these places holds a triangle?
quests.hint: The unit has 4 shapes. Find the place of the triangle in the unit, then keep adding 4.
quests.explanation: The triangle is the 3rd shape in each unit of 4, so it appears in places 3, 7, 11, and so on. The 8th is a circle and the 9th is a square.
quests.funFact: Adding the length of the unit to a place number gives the same shape in the next copy of the unit.

quests.instruction: Which row of shapes looks the same when it is flipped left to right?
quests.hint: Read the row forward, then backward, and compare.
quests.explanation: Read backward, triangle, square, circle, square, triangle is still the same row, so a left to right flip leaves it unchanged.
quests.funFact: Rows like this have a line of symmetry through the middle shape.

quests.instruction: A seven-bead necklace is symmetrical. Its first three beads are red, blue, and green. What color is the fifth bead?
quests.hint: In a symmetrical necklace, the beads on one side match the beads on the other side in reverse order.
quests.explanation: The 5th bead mirrors the 3rd bead, the 6th mirrors the 2nd, and the 7th mirrors the 1st, so the 5th is green.
quests.funFact: The middle bead of a symmetrical necklace with an odd number of beads has no partner.

quests.instruction: A flower design has 6 identical petals spaced evenly around a center. How much of a full turn separates one petal from the next?
quests.hint: Six equal gaps fill a whole turn.
quests.explanation: Six equal gaps make one full turn, so each gap is one sixth of a turn.
quests.funFact: Many flowers have petals arranged this way, so they look the same after one sixth of a turn.

quests.instruction: Which group has shapes that can each cover a floor on their own with no gaps?
quests.correctAnswer: Squares, triangles with equal sides, and regular hexagons
options: Squares, triangles with equal sides, and regular hexagons
quests.hint: Think about which shapes can sit edge to edge without leaving holes.
quests.explanation: Squares, triangles with three equal sides, and regular hexagons all fit edge to edge with no gaps. Circles, ovals, and regular pentagons leave gaps.
quests.funFact: These three shapes appear in tile patterns around the world.

quests.instruction: Why can regular pentagons not cover a floor without gaps?
quests.correctAnswer: Their corners leave gaps where they meet
options: Their corners leave gaps where they meet
quests.hint: Think about what happens where several corners come together at one point.
quests.explanation: Where regular pentagons meet at a point, their corners do not add up to fill all the way around, so gaps are left.
quests.funFact: Some five-sided shapes that are not regular can cover a floor with no gaps.

quests.instruction: A standard checkerboard is 8 by 8, with squares alternating dark and light. How many dark squares does it have?
quests.hint: Dark and light squares alternate, so what fraction of the board is dark?
quests.explanation: The board has 8 × 8 = 64 squares, and half of them are dark, so there are 32 dark squares.
quests.funFact: Draughts, also called checkers, is played on the dark squares only.

quests.instruction: A pattern repeats triangle, square, circle. What is the 15th shape?
quests.hint: 15 is a multiple of 3. Where does a multiple of 3 fall in the unit?
quests.explanation: Every 3rd shape ends a unit, and 15 = 5 × 3, so the 15th shape is the last in its unit, a circle.
quests.funFact: Multiples of the unit length always land on the last shape of a unit.

quests.instruction: A design has 4 lines of symmetry and looks the same after each quarter turn. Which design could it be?
options: A rectangle with two long sides
quests.hint: Look for the design that matches itself after every quarter turn.
quests.explanation: A plus sign folds four ways and looks the same after every quarter turn. A rectangle has 2 lines and matches only after a half turn, and a leaning parallelogram has no lines.
quests.funFact: A square also has four lines of symmetry and matches itself after every quarter turn.

quests.instruction: A pattern has 2, 4, 6, 8 squares in its first four steps. One student says step 5 has 10 squares. Another says it has 16 because the pattern doubles. Who is right?
quests.correctAnswer: The first student, because 2 more are added each time
options: The second student, because it doubles
The first student, because 2 more are added each time
quests.hint: Check each rule against every step, not just the first two.
quests.explanation: From 2 to 4 could be doubling, but 4 to 6 is not. Every step adds 2, so step 5 has 10.
quests.funFact: A rule must work for every step in a pattern, not just the first one or two.
